messages:
maya: quick heads-up — i'm going to flip the inference-gateway svc from ClusterIP -> NodePort for a short canary. need a sanity check on NLB healthcheck behavior + TLS secret wiring before i push the tf change.

aj: why NodePort for the canary? can we do gateway routing only?

maya: we want a blue path that the NLB can target directly for a single-az debug; easier to validate traffic routing. will be temporary.

lucas: note: if you go NodePort, the NLB must target the node port (targetType=nodeport). healthchecks hit the node IP:nodePort unless you're using proxy protocol. also double-check externalTrafficPolicy.

sre-sam: agree. externalTrafficPolicy: Local if you need source IP preserved. but that means you need pods in each AZ (or LB healthchecks will fail if no local endpoint).

maya: snippet i'm planning to apply in terraform: 
```hcl
resource "kubernetes_service" "inference_gw" {
  metadata {
    name = "inference-gateway"
    annotations = {
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type" = "nlb"
      "service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-cross-zone-load-balancing-enabled" = "true"
    }
  }
  spec {
    type = "NodePort"
    external_traffic_policy = "Local"
    ports {
      name = "https"
      port = 443
      target_port = 8080
      # node_port omitted so k8s can pick one
    }
    selector = { app = "inference" }
  }
}
```

aj: two quick calls out: 1) if NLB should terminate TLS (listener cert on LB) we need annotations and ingress config; for passthrough keep it TCP 443 on the LB and let the pod handle TLS. 2) Gateway API TLSSecret binding behavior depends on the controller (contour, istio, etc.) — confirm which Gateway controller we run.

lucas: also add readinessProbe on 8080 (/healthz) so the node is marked healthy for NLB checks. Without readiness probe the NLB can mark instances unhealthy even if nodePort exists.

sre-sam: on TLS secret wiring: if you want LB termination use the AWS cert ARN on the service annotation (if using service-controller that supports it). For passthrough, keep secret in the namespace the gateway/listener expects. Gateway API requires TLS cert refs to be in same namespace as the Gateway or be a SecretNameReference depending on controller.

maya: we're using gateway-api with aws-load-balancer-controller for the NLB. plan is TCP passthrough to pods (so pods must have TLS certs). secrets are in namespace infra-tls. does the Gateway accept cross-namespace secretRef with our controller?

aj: aws-lb-controller doesn't manage Gateway TLS secrets for passthrough — Gateway controller (gateway-api implementer) handles that. iirc our gateway controller disallows cross-namespace secretRefs by default. simplest is to keep TLS secret in the same namespace as the Gateway resource.

lucas: if you can't move secrets, another option is to create a copy of the secret in the gateway namespace and annotate it with ownership for automated sync (we have a small helper script for that).

maya: ok i'll either copy the secret or move it. also will add readinessProbe and ensure pod replicas >= number of AZs because of externalTrafficPolicy=Local.

sre-sam: one more: if you remove hardcoded nodePort (recommended), k8s assigns one — NLB TargetGroup will pick it up via the service controller. only specify nodePort if you need a stable port for firewall rules.

maya: good call, i'll remove explicit nodePort.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] terraform plan queued by maya (plan id: 3124).

aj: i'll take a look at the PR after standup. pls include the readinessProbe change in the same PR.

maya: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
